category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a UK council booking service: GOV.UK-like single column, bold sans headings, institutional green or blue accent, 'There is a problem' red-bordered error summary, step list, white summary card. Predicted opposite: a friendly rounded consumer look with illustration. Every identity-carrying element (ground, accent, type voice, error pattern, summary card) matches the default.

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'booking for a council household waste site in another district, residents on phones'. Predicted choices: council green, system/humanist sans, tile grid of times with availability tags, Morning/Afternoon grouping, summary list with Change links, plain confirmation with a reference. Overlap is near total.

findings.title: Cancelled booking page still says 'Booked' and tells the resident to show the reference at the gate
findings.description: On done.html with status=cancelled, the H1 remains 'Booked', and below the red 'Status: cancelled. This booking is not on the gate's list.' the card still says 'Show this at the gate, on your phone or on paper...' and 'A reminder will be sent to your mobile the evening before.' The page contradicts itself; the largest text says the opposite of the status.
findings.impact: A resident glancing at the page (the scene is a phone, often while doing something else) may read 'Booked' and the gate instructions and drive to the centre, to be turned away.

harm.statement: Residents whose booking is cancelled may take this page as a live booking because the heading says 'Booked' and the text tells them to show it at the gate, and may arrive and be turned away.

evidence.detail: H1 'Booked'; red status line; 'Show this at the gate'; 'A reminder will be sent'.

findings.recommendation: Decide what the cancelled state must say first and make the heading and the instructions follow that state.

findings.title: Done page shows the reference but not the day, slot or vehicle that were booked
findings.description: The done page lists 'Your reference DR-204117' and generic 'At the centre' text but omits the booked day (Saturday 17 October), slot (09:20 to 09:40) and vehicle, all of which were shown on the confirm page.
findings.impact: The page's job is to 'know the booking is made and what to show at the gate'; the resident cannot check from it when to arrive, and the gate checks the vehicle against the booking.

harm.statement: Residents reading this page the evening before (or at the gate with no signal) cannot see which day and 20-minute slot they booked, so they may arrive at the wrong time.
harm.requirement: context.md (PRODUCT.md) surfaces: done — 'know the booking is made and what to show at the gate'

evidence.detail: Reference card has no date, slot or vehicle.
No day/slot/vehicle on done default at 375-dark or 1280-light, though the route carries date=2026-10-17&slot=09:20&vehicle=car.

findings.recommendation: Decide what the gate and the resident need on one screen and show the booking details with the reference.

findings.title: 'Few left' slots are pulled into an unlabelled group above Morning, out of time order
findings.description: On the when page, slots with few places (08:20 to 16:40) are gathered into a group with no heading above 'Morning', so the Morning group reads 08:00, 09:20, 10:00, 11:00 and Afternoon starts at 12:00 with gaps. Time order across the day is broken into two parallel lists.
findings.impact: Residents scanning 'Saturday morning' under the Morning heading see fewer morning slots than exist and may pick a worse time or another day; the amber group takes the second fixation without saying what it is.

harm.statement: Residents looking for a morning slot may read the Morning group as the complete list and miss 08:20, 08:40, 09:00, 09:40, 10:20 and 10:40, which sit in the unlabelled group above.

evidence.detail: Ten 'Few left' tiles above 'Morning'; Morning shows 08:00, 09:20, 10:00, 11:00-11:40.

findings.recommendation: Decide whether scarcity or time is the organising order; if time, keep each slot in its time group and let the tag carry scarcity.

findings.title: Expired slot: summary shows '–' while 'Book this slot' stays the filled primary
findings.description: On confirm with hold=expired, the error box says 'This slot is no longer available.' and the summary's Slot row shows '–', yet 'Book this slot' remains the single filled button and the error box offers no route back to choosing a slot (only the small 'Change slot' link in the card).
findings.impact: The primary action points at something that cannot succeed; the recovery step is the smallest link on the page.

harm.statement: Residents whose hold expired are steered to press 'Book this slot' again rather than to choose a new slot, adding a failed attempt before they find 'Change slot'.

evidence.detail: Error box with no link; Slot '–'; filled 'Book this slot' at y≈1097.

findings.recommendation: Decide which action the expired state's one filled button should be, and put the way back to the slots where the error is read.

findings.title: Permit number field appears before a van or trailer is chosen
findings.description: On vehicle.html in the errors and info-open states, no vehicle is selected but the 'Permit number' field with 'Starts DRC-, then five digits.' is shown under the vehicle choice.
findings.impact: Most residents bring a car and do not need a permit; a visible permit field suggests they do.

harm.statement: Car drivers (the primary group) may think they need a permit number to book and stop to look for one.

evidence.detail: No vehicle selected; permit field shown.
No vehicle selected; permit field shown.

findings.recommendation: Decide when the permit question applies and show it only then, with the rule beside it.

findings.title: No signature or identity beyond the masthead line; the frame could serve any booking service
findings.description: Every identity-carrying element (pale ground, white bordered cards, institutional green, one sans, tile grid, red error summary) is the category default; the only mark is a bin outline and the council name in bold body text. The done-page reference, the one thing residents carry to the gate, is an ordinary heading in a white card.
findings.impact: Design note: the service reads as a template rather than the council's own; nothing gives the 'plain, not bare' attribute its 'not bare' half.
findings.recommendation: Decide one element from the centre's own world (the gate check, the reference read on a phone with poor signal) to carry the identity quietly on every surface.

findings.title: Half-empty full-width cards and a short grid leave empty right halves at wide widths
findings.description: At 1280/1440 the 'Your booking', 'Your reference' and 'Opening days' cards span ~1088px with content in the left third, while forms are 610px and the slot grid ~720px; on done at 1280 an empty band of page ground sits under the footer.
findings.impact: Design note: two column widths fight on each page and the boxes look unfinished on desktop.
findings.recommendation: Decide one content width per step and keep cards, grid and form on it.

findings.title: Two visual styles for the same choose-one control (day buttons vs vehicle boxes)
findings.description: Day buttons use bold green text with a green border; vehicle boxes use regular dark text with a grey border, and the selected vehicle is marked mainly by bolder text and border.
findings.impact: Design note: the same kind of choice looks different from step to step.
findings.recommendation: Decide one treatment for single-choice controls and their selected state.

strengths: Rules are written beside the control they govern ('Starts DRC-, then five digits', 'Rubble (up to four bags)') in the gate attendant's plain voice.
One filled primary per step and a composed (not inverted) dark theme with readable mint actions.
keep: Keep the plain, firm, second-person copy and the one-filled-button-per-step discipline.
not_assessable: Motion, hover and focus behaviour, the toast and keyboard order cannot be judged from stills. No baseline screenshots, so no pairwise comparison.
